subject: Information Theory
title: Satellite Internet
description: A micro-lesson that makes Satellite Internet usable.

hook.text: Starlink has over 5,000 satellites orbiting at 550 km. They beam internet to places no cable could ever reach.

buildup.text: Low-Earth orbit satellites reduce latency to 20-40 ms. Geostationary satellites at 36,000 km add 600 ms of delay.

discovery.text: Satellite constellations form a mesh network in space. Laser links between satellites route data without ground relay.

twist.text: Spectrum sharing between satellites and ground systems is an information-theoretic puzzle: everyone shares the same sky.

climax.text: Satellite internet extends Shannon's channel to three dimensions. The information network now wraps the entire planet.

punchline.text: No cables needed. The sky becomes the network.

quiz.question: Why do low-Earth orbit satellites have lower latency?
options: Their shorter distance reduces signal travel time
